review.summary: This paper presents TRD (Toroidal Rank Decoding), a method for generating 16x16 tileable pixel-art textures conditioned on a material name and target region colour. The approach factors textures into a 16-slot palette and an NxN grid of luminance ranks, decoding them via an iterative masked generative transformer without absolute position embeddings. Spatial tileability and cyclic-shift equivariance are enforced using a parameter-light toroidal relative attention bias based on Fourier harmonic features, while colour palettes are retrieved from a training memory and shifted in Lab space. Evaluated on 272 held-out materials from game texture packs, TRD achieves superior KID and FID compared to render-and-downsample and pixel diffusion baselines, running in 0.51 s per tile.
strengths: Principled formulation of pixel-art representation that decouples structure (luminance rank grid) from color (palette indices), matching domain authoring practices.
Elegant and parameter-efficient implementation of toroidal relative attention bias (Eq. 2) that guarantees exact cyclic shift equivariance by construction without seam artifacts.
Exceptional generation speed (0.51 s per tile end-to-end), representing a 28x speedup over period-cropped SDXL rendering and over 30,000x over score distillation (SD-piXL).

Exemplary metric hygiene in Section 5: explicitly measuring resampling noise floors, identifying pathological boundary cases in standard tiling scores, and benchmarking judge resolvable-rate floors on identical pairs.

weaknesses.point: The generative model cannot generate realistic palettes end-to-end; texture quality depends heavily on retrieving memorized artist palettes from the training set. In Table 5, removing the palette memory and relying on the model's palette head causes KID to collapse from 9.7 to 35.1 and FID from 44.2 to 68.2 (with judge preference dropping to 66.3%). This undermines the claim of fully generative native synthesis, functioning instead as a retrieval-augmented rank inpainter.
weaknesses.what_would_fix_it: Clarify throughout the abstract and introduction that the system is a hybrid retrieval-generative pipeline rather than an end-to-end texture generator, and investigate conditional palette generation models (e.g., discrete diffusion over palette codes) that do not depend on exact training palette retrieval.

weaknesses.point: The evaluation dataset exhibits almost complete semantic overlap with the training set. As noted in Section 3 (line 161), 448 of the 450 test materials occur in the training split under different artists. While packs/artists are held out, open-vocabulary generalization to unseen material categories and arbitrary prompt compositions is essentially unverified.
weaknesses.what_would_fix_it: Evaluate TRD on a curated benchmark of truly out-of-distribution material names and prompt compositions that never appear in the training ContentDB (e.g., modern, sci-fi, synthetic, or composite concepts).

weaknesses.point: Performance deteriorates when scaling to higher resolutions. In Table 7 (Appendix C), TRD+rr is decisively outperformed by the period-cropped render baseline B2 at 32x32 (win rate 41.1%, p=0.014, family CI [0.315, 0.502]), and only ties B2 at 24x24 (50.0%). Furthermore, at 16x16, single-sample TRD without reranking loses to B2 (47.4%, Table 7), indicating that TRD's competitive edge is narrow and resolution-bounded.
weaknesses.what_would_fix_it: Acknowledge the resolution scaling limits in the main text rather than relegating B2's win at 32x32 to Appendix C, and analyze why discrete rank decoding loses fidelity relative to downscaled continuous diffusion representations as grid dimensions grow.

weaknesses.point: The comparison against the primary published low-resolution quantized generative baseline, SD-piXL (B3), is evaluated on only 12 materials (Table 3, line 347). An n=12 sample size lacks statistical power, prevents the computation of family-level confidence intervals, and is insufficient to draw firm conclusions against the literature.
weaknesses.what_would_fix_it: Expand the evaluation of SD-piXL (or a computationally feasible accelerated score distillation variant) to at least 40-50 materials across multiple distinct families to enable robust confidence interval reporting.

weaknesses.point: The human ground truth study used to calibrate the VLM judge is underspecified in Section 5. The paper mentions four annotators evaluating 60 pairs, but omits inter-annotator agreement metrics (e.g., Fleiss' kappa), annotator qualifications/domain expertise, and protocol instructions.
weaknesses.what_would_fix_it: Provide complete reporting of the human validation study in Appendix A, including inter-annotator agreement scores, instructions provided to annotators, and full details on the filtering criteria for candidate VLM judges.

questions: How does TRD perform on novel material names that have low cosine similarity to any material in the training-set palette memory?

Why does the performance of TRD degrade against B2 at 32x32 (41.1% win rate in Table 7)? Is this due to the capacity of the 33M transformer, the F=8 harmonic representation, or the MaskGIT decoding schedule on larger token grids?
Could you report the inter-annotator agreement (e.g., Cohen's or Fleiss' kappa) for the 4 human annotators on the 60-pair validation set?
In Table 5, why does choice temperature 20 yield better results than 4.5? Does high stochasticity during early decoding steps prevent premature commitment to bad structural layouts?
